stem: Acidic chyme entering the duodenum stimulates secretion of which of the following hormones?

options.label: A
options.misconception: The gastric acid stimulator is being assigned to the duodenal acid signal.
options.explanation: Gastrin is released when food enters the stomach; acidic chyme in the duodenum triggers secretin, not gastrin.

options.label: B
options.misconception: None; acidic chyme is the secretin stimulus.
options.explanation: Secretin is released when acidic chyme reaches the duodenum and drives bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice to neutralize the acid.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Both the hormone and its source are wrong for an acid stimulus.
options.explanation: CCK responds to protein and fat in the duodenum, not to acid alone, and it is not secreted by parietal cells.

options.label: D
options.misconception: A motility hormone is being substituted for the acid-neutralizing hormone.
options.explanation: Motilin initiates migrating motor complexes; acidic chyme triggers secretin for bicarbonate secretion.

options.label: E
options.misconception: A glucose-regulating islet hormone is being inserted into intestinal phase digestion.
options.explanation: Glucagon regulates blood glucose; duodenal acid activates secretin to coordinate pancreatic bicarbonate release.

context: Learning objective: match acidic chyme to secretin. Secretin from duodenal mucosa triggers bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice; protein and fat later stimulate CCK for enzyme release.
